agents.name: Claude Code
agents.quote: I have a GCP VM for Claude Code, and also a Mac Mini that bridges dev and prod, sort of a "corp network."

surface_source.quote: By consolidating all my terminal windows into a single rolodex that I can flip through, I freed up my desktop for real work.

agents.name: Codex
agents.quote: I also have a small parallel fleet of five named Sol 5.6 workers on Codex, all named for sun gods. I use it as a fallback for when my Max accounts run out, which is increasingly often, despite me adding new ones once or twice a week.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.quote: I first switched most of my seats to Fable 5.1 (my headless Aesop reviewer pool is still Fable 5)

history.quote: Opus 4.5 can handle any reasonably sized task, so your job is to make tasks for it.

models.name: Opus 5
models.quote: My fleet, all Opus 5 agents, are the work consumers, like Gas Town's polecats, but non-ephemeral.

review_style.value: Fable reviews every Opus change; he doesn't read code
review_style.quote: Every implementation bead goes through this lifecycle: Fable design, Opus implementation, Fable review.

also.quote: And as another appetizer, human code review has very nearly run its course.
I’ve never seen the code, and I never care to, which might give you pause.

harness.value: Wheelhouse, all in Emacs, tmux underneath, Beads on Dolt
harness.quote: I began the journey inside Emacs, so Wheelhouse has been all-Emacs from the ground up.

history.quote: Gas Town uses tmux as its primary UI.

parallelism.quote: But with Fable's latest "25%" pricing, which is yet another cut, my Wheelhouse factory is now mostly idling.

history.quote: I’ve tamed them to where you can use 20–30 at once, productively, on a sustained basis.
Wheelhouse has 50 agents that are amnesiac and interchangeable, and the only way they can coordinate is via text.

rules_files.value: AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md points to it), beads for all tasks
rules_files.quote: Do NOT batch multiple fixes. Do NOT wait until "end of session". Push immediately after each completed task.

mcp_servers.quote: I run pretty lean. I don't use any sandboxing. I don't use MCP.

signature.caption: 18 long-lived Fable officers
signature.why: Our pick: every agent boots into a named office with its own memory and authority, which he says saves tokens.
signature.quote: Seats are your most fundamental and powerful building block for agentic workflows, whether you're building orchestrators or not.

archetype.why: 50 agents: a Fable crew designs and reviews, Opus builds.

signature_quote.value: human code review has very nearly run its course.
signature_quote.more: Its vestigial SOC 2 compliance angle will keep it on life support, but by next year, human code review is completely done and gone.
